stories.headline: Trumbull boys soccer blanks Simsbury 1–0 in Sunday Soccer Challenge
stories.summary: Trumbull kept a clean sheet Sunday and edged Simsbury 1–0 in the Soccer Challenge matchup that had been waiting on a final overnight. MaxPreps has the Eagles at 6–3–1 (1–2–1 since a three-game win streak ended) and ranked 21st in Connecticut, well ahead of the Trojans (1–5–4, ranked 112th). Both sides hit the road next — Trumbull at McMahon Wednesday at 5:30 p.m., Simsbury at Conard Thursday.

stories.headline: Westport: Jesup Road bridge out 12–18 months; EMS tests say only slight delay
stories.summary: Westport’s Jesup Road bridge, wrecked by the Sept. 13 flash flood, must be replaced rather than repaired — Public Works estimates 12–18 months even with expedited permitting. Police say patrol response is unaffected, but EMS and Volunteer EMS dispatch from the Jesup Road headquarters; First Selectman Kevin Christie said EMS Chief Patrick Riddle’s timed runs found roughly 30 seconds to one minute extra only for calls on Imperial Avenue south of the closure. The town is seeking state and federal help and may demolish the compromised span soon.

stories.headline: Breece Hall headed for Monday MRI after thigh injury ends Jets’ late collapse
stories.summary: Breece Hall left Sunday’s 31–24 loss in Detroit clutching his right thigh and told reporters he felt something while running, then again when he planted — and that an MRI is likely Monday. Garrett Wilson cleared concussion protocol after a late hit; left guard Dylan Parham (knee) did not return. Geno Smith’s 321 yards and three touchdowns fueled a 24–10 comeback before Jahmyr Gibbs’ late score and a strip-sack sealed New York’s second straight late defeat at 1–2.

stories.headline: Penguins: Lizotte back at full-contact practice — IR may not block opener
stories.summary: Blake Lizotte (upper-body, day-to-day) returned to full-contact practice Sunday in his usual fourth-line center spot even as Pittsburgh listed him, Justin Brazeau, Ben Kindel and Ryan Graves on IR ahead of Wednesday’s opener in Philadelphia. Pro Hockey Rumors notes the IR move may not keep Lizotte out of the Flyers game if he keeps progressing; Brazeau and Kindel are week-to-week and Graves (knee) is out indefinitely while Bryan Rust, Tristan Broz and Andrei Kuzmenko remain cloudy.

stories.headline: Trump: White House ‘very seriously’ considering diesel export ban as prices soar
stories.summary: Speaking Sunday at the Presidents Cup, President Trump told Fox the White House is still “thinking about it very seriously” and “may do” a diesel export restriction as U.S. retail diesel hovers near record highs around $6.50 a gallon ahead of the midterms. Energy Secretary Chris Wright has floated limits rather than a full ban; analysts and the American Petroleum Institute warn refiners could cut runs and lift gasoline prices, while Europe — which has leaned on U.S. cargoes for roughly half its recent diesel imports — would face a sharper squeeze.

stories.headline: DHS: assaults on ICE up more than 1,700% vs Biden’s first 21 months
stories.summary: Homeland Security data cited by The Center Square count 647 assaults on ICE officers in the first 21 months of Trump’s second term versus 37 in the same Biden window — more than a 1,700% jump — with death threats up even more sharply. Secretary Markwayne Mullin blamed “vicious lies” from sanctuary politicians; the roundup lists finger-biting and Molotov attacks from Minneapolis to Los Angeles, vehicle-dragging and Tren de Aragua assaults, white-powder mailings, and Texas facility shootings, as Sen. John Cornyn’s ICE Protection Act seeks tougher penalties.

stories.headline: Matt Walsh: ‘Good for Jonathan Majors’ for refusing to cave on Infidels role
stories.summary: After Jonathan Majors defended starring in Daily Wire’s campus-terror thriller Run Hide Fight: Infidels, Matt Walsh praised the actor for “refusing to cave” amid backlash over the film’s portrayal of Islamist violence at a protest encampment. Majors told Daily Wire subscribers he reads scripts for character responsibility, director vision, and whether the material asks questions he cannot already answer — and said he wanted the Clay Saunders role to grow as an artist. The sequel landed Sept. 16 on Daily Wire’s platform to polarized reviews.

stories.headline: Jeep recalls ~97,000 Wagoneer SUVs after roof crossbars can detach
stories.summary: FCA US is recalling 97,349 Jeep Wagoneer and Grand Wagoneer models (2022–2026, including L variants) because under-torqued roof-rack pivot bolts can let a crossbar detach and become a road hazard. NHTSA’s report cites rattling or a missing bolt as owner clues; FCA found 15 related warranty claims worldwide and no known crashes or injuries as of late August. Dealers were notified around Sept. 17; owners get interim notices starting Oct. 8 while redesigned remedy bolts are prepared — check your VIN on NHTSA.gov.

stories.headline: Starship Flight 14: Monday window open for first orbital try with 26 Starlink V3s
stories.summary: Spaceflight Now’s Monday live coverage frames Starship Flight 14 (booster B21 / Ship 41) as the program’s first attempt at a sustained Earth orbit, with a 75-minute window opening 8:15 a.m. ET from Starbase. If the ~25-minute insertion burn succeeds, Ship 41 would deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites starting about 34 minutes after liftoff, complete roughly six orbits, then splash down off western South America — with no recovery of either stage and a possible Ship catch deferred to Flight 15.

stories.headline: Inmo Air3 smart glasses recalled after overheating temples cause burns
stories.summary: Inmo is recalling more than 1,600 Air3 smart glasses sold in the U.S. and Canada after the left temple can overheat in extended use — a burn hazard the CPSC ties to 10 reports of burning on the face and left ear. Units sold Dec. 2025–Aug. 2026 for $900–$1,300 via Inmo, Amazon and Kickstarter carry an Air3/Inmo label on the right temple. Owners should stop using them immediately and contact Inmo for a free firmware update; earlier reviews had already flagged the heat and a protective sleeve bundled with the glasses.
